description: Grammar shapes that used to be syntax errors: a lambda body carrying NOT, AND or a NOT-of-function-call; CASE arms whose THEN or ELSE is a bare boolean expression (searched and simple forms alike) beside the ordinary value-returning CASE; a WITH clause before SELECT ... INTO inside a procedure; CTAS with a TYPED column list, a multi-column typed list and the names-only list; a reserved keyword as a VARIANT path key; DO usable as a table alias and column qualifier without breaking WHILE ... DO; and trailing commas in the FROM list and in the select list together. Converted 1:1 from features/SyntaxGapCoverageTest (now retired).

steps.sql: SELECT FILTER([1, 2, 3, 4], x -> NOT (x > 2))

skip.reason: the HTTP transport re-serialises an ARRAY cell through its own JSON writer, which emits '[1, 2]' with a space after each comma where the engine and JDBC render the compact '[1,2]'; the FILTER result itself is identical, only its transport rendering differs

skip.reason: the HTTP transport re-serialises an ARRAY cell through its own JSON writer, which emits '[1, 2]' with a space after each comma where the engine and JDBC render the compact '[1,2]'; the FILTER result itself is identical, only its transport rendering differs

CREATE OR REPLACE TEMPORARY TABLE ct_typed (ITEM_CODE VARCHAR) AS SELECT UPPER('abc') AS x
SELECT ITEM_CODE FROM ct_typed
SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'CT_TYPED'
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ct_multi (a NUMBER(10,0), b VARCHAR) AS SELECT 5, 'hi'
SELECT a, b FROM ct_multi
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ct_names (nm, tot) AS SELECT 'x', 9
SELECT nm, tot FROM ct_names
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE vk (src VARIANT)
INSERT INTO vk SELECT OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('account', OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('status', 'OK'))
SELECT src:account.status::VARCHAR FROM vk
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE dt (region_id INTEGER, item_code INTEGER)
INSERT INTO dt VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20)
SELECT do.region_id, do.item_code FROM dt do WHERE do.region_id = 1
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tca (id INTEGER)
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tcb (id INTEGER)
INSERT INTO tca VALUES (1), (2)
INSERT INTO tcb VALUES (1)
SELECT tca.id FROM tca, tcb, WHERE tca.id = tcb.id
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tcc (a INTEGER, b INTEGER)
INSERT INTO tcc VALUES (7, 8)
SELECT a, b, FROM tcc, WHERE a = 7
